ABOUT MATTER LABS

Matter Labs builds infrastructure for financial sovereignty. We pioneered zero-knowledge rollups on Ethereum and developed the Prividium platform to help financial institutions build and operate digital asset businesses with privacy and control.
The platform’s adoption spans global finance, from DTCC, a cornerstone of securities markets, to Cari’s network of 30 banks representing $10 trillion in combined assets.

We’re a remote, global team tackling hard problems in cryptography and finance. Expect autonomy, high standards and access to the best AI tools. Your work will help shape how financial institutions move and manage money.




THE ROLE

You join the Platform team, which designs and builds the ZKsync OS node. You own one or more of its core systems end to end: peer-to-peer networking, consensus, RPC, the sequencer or storage, depending on where your depth is. We are looking first for depth in consensus or peer-to-peer networking, and next in high-performance storage. You also bring new protocol features into the node, such as cross-chain interoperability and new zero-knowledge provers.

The Production Unit runs the node for customers, and the Platform team makes sure what it runs is correct. The role has no customer-facing work. When an incident touches a system you own, the Production Unit can pull you in during your working hours.

What you will do:

 - Own core node systems. Design, build and maintain one or more of networking, consensus, RPC, sequencing or storage, and decide how they evolve.

 - Integrate new protocol features. Bring features such as interoperability and new provers into the node without breaking existing behaviour or the upgrade path.

 - Design bugs out. Use the type system, architecture, property-based testing and fuzzing so whole classes of bugs never reach production.

 - Hold the review bar. Review your colleagues' code as carefully as you write your own, and expect the same from them.

 - Use AI with judgment. Use the best AI tools to move faster, and understand every line you merge, whoever or whatever wrote it.

Within a year, you own one or two of the node's core systems, and features land in them without regressions.




WHAT WE LOOK FOR

 - You have designed and built a core component of a distributed system, blockchain node or database: networking, consensus, storage, an RPC layer or similar.

 - You write strong systems code in Rust, C++, Go or a comparable language. Our node is written in Rust, and Rust is learnable here.

 - You use types and architecture to make invalid states unrepresentable, and you have used property-based testing or fuzzing on real code.

 - Your code reviews find real problems, and you can explain every line you ship.

 - You can take a protocol change from specification to a running system without breaking what already works.

Nice to have: Ethereum execution or consensus client internals; RocksDB or another high-performance storage engine; zero-knowledge provers; libp2p or a comparable networking stack; open-source systems work we can read.

If you meet most of this and the rest is learnable, apply anyway.





COMPENSATION AND WORK MODEL

 - Base salary range: USD 150,000 to 187,000 per year. Where an offer lands in the range depends on demonstrated scope and results against the bar described above. The same range applies wherever you are based.

 - Performance-based variable compensation and a long-term token incentive are additional.

 - Benefits (employees): medical, dental and vision from day one, global health cover for team members outside the US; 401(k) with a Safe Harbor match up to 4 percent for eligible US employees, flexible paid time off plus public holidays and two company closure weeks a year; six weeks paid parental bonding leave plus up to ten weeks paid birth recovery leave; confidential mental health support; a USD 2,000 home office stipend, a company laptop refreshed every three years, up to USD 400 a month toward coworking, and a USD 500 annual learning budget; company and team offsites.

 - Fully remote, from any country where we can hire. Your working hours overlap with European or US time zones. Time zones close to Europe fit the team best.

 - Full-time, as an employee or a contractor.

**About Us**
Chariot Defense is a defense technology company that designs and manufactures a family of power products for the U.S. military and its allies. We believe that credible deterrence of armed conflict and winning if deterrence fails, requires more than just the best drones, sensors, weapons, electronic warfare systems, and command & control capabilities. Those critical components will require sustained electric power in austere and resource-constrained environments. Moreover, military units must be able to turn off the trucks and generators that generate this power to hide and survive. In other words, power generation must be decoupled from power consumption. Chariot Defense’s products enable exactly this capability, allowing U.S. and allied militaries to be more lethal and survivable. We hope you will join us on this mission.
  
  
**About the Role**
We're looking for an Embedded Linux Engineer to own that software platform from the ground up, taking a bare, custom-built board and getting Linux to boot and run reliably on it, then keeping that stack maintainable as we ship and update units in the field. You’ll be the engineer responsible for embedded platforms are built, deployed, and updated across Amphora and future products. Our team comes from Tesla, Anduril, Apple, Archer, and the U.S. military, and we're already fielded across DoD exercises. This is a high-ownership, hands-on role that sits right at the hardware-software boundary.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Board bring-up: Take freshly fabricated carrier boards from freshly assembled to reliably booting — methodically proving out power, memory, and communication interfaces, hands-on with hardware on the bench.
* Bootloader & kernel configuration: Stand up the bootloader and configure the Linux kernel so it correctly recognizes and drives our specific hardware.
* Device drivers & device tree: Describe our custom hardware to Linux and integrate the drivers needed to talk to peripherals that aren't found in any standard catalog.
* Build & deploy with Nix / NixOS: Own our operating system defined as code — producing reproducible, identical images and building safe update and rollback paths for fielded units.
* Networking & system services: Configure on-device networking and the system services our higher-level software depends on.
* Reliability & maintainability: Build the platform so it stays robust and serviceable across the product's life, under the conditions a defense product actually faces.
* Cross-functional integration: Partner closely with the firmware and hardware teams, sitting at the seam between low-level hardware and the software that runs on top of it.

**What We’re Looking For**

* Top-notch engineering intuition and first principles thinking toward designing complex products that function seamlessly for your customer, taking both an engineering/ technical, and product/ customer approach, to strike the optimal balance.
* Able to independently identify critical information or priority gaps and apply effort toward closing those gaps.
* Undaunted by imperfect, incomplete or absent datasets or information, and capable of making sound, comprehensive, and swift first-principled decisions to achieve a product end-state that meets and/or exceeds the need of the hour.
* Not satisfied by superficial explanations of a problem or “band-aid engineering”; seeks persistently to find the specific root cause through data-driven methods, and resolve failures or recurring issues, so they can be mitigated to prevent future such instances.
* Gratified by helping your peers succeed, building a robust team culture, and propagation deep camaraderie amongst your peers; seeks to break down information silos by collaborating rigorously with others to solve problems, share knowledge, and provide input.

**Qualifications**
**Required**
:
  
  

* BS in Computer Science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, or equivalent demonstrated experience.
* 3+ years building and shipping embedded Linux on custom hardware.
* Proven board bring-up experience, from powered-off to reliably booting.
* Hands-on with the boot chain: bootloader, kernel configuration, drivers, and device tree.
* Fluent in C/C++ and the embedded Linux toolchain (cross-compilation, JTAG, serial debug).
* Exposure to embedded communication interfaces (CAN, SPI, I2C, UART) at the OS and driver level.

**Preferred**
:
  
  

* Experience with Nix/NixOS.
* Experience with OS configuration as code, Yocto, Ansible.
* Production Rust experience.
* Familiarity with ARM SoCs/SoMs on custom carrier boards.
* Background in automotive, aerospace, defense, robotics, or energy.

**Role Requirements**

* This position is an onsite role based in Chariot Defense’s San Bruno, CA, office.
* Willingness to support 10% travel, domestically and internationally, as well as work extended and weekend hours, when necessary.

A reasonable estimate of the current salary range is $130,000-$180,000 annually. Compensation packages also include early-stage equity and access to company-sponsored benefit plans.
  
  
Individual compensation packages are based on geographic location, scope of the role, relevant experience, and the ability to deal with complexity and problem solve within our organization, among other factors.

**Description**
We are reinventing how Amazon’s builders and security engineers handle security review and issue management. The Security Automation team owns the automations and agentic experiences at the center of that work. We build new systems, integrate with existing ones, and build the services that power our agents. Our goal is to help builders and security engineers understand the security posture of a service quickly and with confidence, and to build tools that automatically fix security vulnerabilities.
  
  
As a Software Development Engineer II, you will own the design and delivery of major pieces of this work, such as the services behind our agents, new automations, and the integrations that connect them to existing systems. You will take problems that are not fully defined, design the solution, and take it to production. You will also help set the technical direction for your area and mentor other engineers on the team.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Design, build, and operate features and components of agentic experiences, from requirements through production.
* Write design documents for your area, evaluate tradeoffs, and make sound decisions on scalability, reliability, and maintainability.
* Build new systems and integrate with existing ones to reduce security overhead and speed up issue resolution.
* Work backwards from customers, partnering with your team and stakeholders to turn ambiguous problems into well scoped solutions.
* Write high quality, well tested code, and review the code and designs of your peers.
* Take part in the on call rotation and drive operational excellence for the systems you own.
* Mentor less experienced engineers and help raise the team’s engineering bar.

A day in the life
  
  
You spend most of your time designing and building. You work through designs with your teammates, write and review code, talk with the customers who use what you build, and keep the systems you own healthy in production.
  
  
**About The Team**
Amazon Security Experiences (ASE) helps Amazon’s builders ship software securely. Our team, Security Automation, builds the automation and agentic experiences that bring this directly to builders and security engineers, so that securing software becomes continuous and increasingly automated. We are early, we are ambitious, and we are reinventing how one of the world’s largest software organizations ships securely.
  
  
Diverse Experiences
  
  
Amazon Security Experiences values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
  
  
Why Amazon Security?
  
  
At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.
  
  
Inclusive Team Culture

Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices.
  
  
Mentorship and Career Growth
  
  
We care about your career growth and strive to assign projects based on what will help each team member develop into a better rounded professional and enable them to take on more complex tasks in the future. You will find endless knowledge sharing, training, and other career advancing resources here.
  
  
Work/Life Balance
  
  
We value work life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there is nothing we can’t achieve.

* 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
* 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
* 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
* Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field

* 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience

**The Culture**
Here at the Institute for Experiential AI (EAI) we are committed to the highest standards in all we do. Working at the EAI offers opportunities, an environment, and a culture that just isn’t found together anywhere else. This is the right place for you if you’re curious, motivated by the future of technology, and want to be part of a unique and diverse community that works on high-impact research, educational, business, and societal problems.
  
  
**Position Summary**
Northeastern University's Institute for Experiential AI is opening an ML engineer with special focus on physical AI systems, knowledge aggregation and AI for control and optimization for a DOE Genesis project led by Dr. Ayan Paul. The ML Engineer will be based at the Boston campus, MA, conduct applied research, prepare work for submission to journal/conference publications, and contribute to extramural funding applications. The ML Engineer will work on projects that will include developing AI models for signal processing. Participation in this project will include scientific programming, data analysis, training AI models, manuscript preparation, meeting with collaborators, mentoring graduate students, etc.
  
  
About the project: CLARA (Cognitive Layered Agentic Reasoning for ARIS) is a three-year, Genesis Mission Phase II project led by Northeastern University with MSU/FRIB and Gravitate AI. It will build an agentic AI system for operating the Advanced Rare Isotope Separator (ARIS) at FRIB. ARIS operations are limited by the gap between LISE++ simulations and observed beam behavior. As a result, weekly beam development takes 16 to 24 hours, about half of which goes to manual isotope calibration. Planning a new experiment takes about 20 days, and no predictive monitoring exists for roughly 200 time-correlated machine parameters.
  
  
**CLARA Addresses This With Three Objectives**

* Planning and tuning. Bayesian optimization uses LISE++ as a physics-informed prior, alongside paired forward and inverse neural surrogates trained on simulation and EPICS archive data. These power a Planning Agent for non-experts and an Expert Tuning Agent.
* Calibration. Diffeomorphic image registration maps simulated particle identification (PID) distributions to measured ones from a single measurement.
* Monitoring and knowledge. Quickest Change Detection models (classical CuSum and a transformer-based DeepQCD) and a hazardous-configuration classifier make up a Safety Agent with gated beam-interrupt authority. A Critic module commits validated tunes to a knowledge graph built with eGoT.

The targets are reducing experiment planning time to 1 to 2 days, beam development time to about 4 hours, and thus facilitating 500 to 800 extra beam hours per year. The project aims to advance from TRL 3 to TRL 6–7 and to validate transfer to at least one non-ARIS separator. The ML Engineer hired for this position will work with Benjamin Gyori at Khoury College, Deniz Erdogmus at the College of Engineering, and Ayan Paul at EAI and is expected to develop AI algorithms, RAG pipelines and agentic systems for the Genesis project, collaborate with the FRIB experiment at the Michigan State University and Gravitate AI.
  
  
**Qualifications**

* MS in Computer Science, Data Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, or related fields or currently enrolled in a master’s program.
* A minimum of 3-4 years of experience working with ML/AI (TensorFlow/Pytorch) and ETL pipelines.
* Proficiency in Python and R. Experienced with Unix and remote computing clusters.
* Having experience in wrangling large datasets, building databases and ETL is preferred.
* An ability to write clean and well-documented code and work with GitHub repositories.
* Experience in signal processing in the spaciotemporal domain.
* Excellent organizational skills including attention to detail and multitasking.
* An ability to troubleshoot and problem-solve in response to challenges, especially, in an iar domain.
* Experience with AWS is a plus but not required. Experience with high performance computing is preferred.

**Values & Abilities**

* Excellent written and verbal communication skills and ability to communicate effectively with a variety of different stakeholders from various academic backgrounds.
* Respect for diversity and the importance of interdisciplinary teams.
* Self-starter and innovative thinker and a team-player who can collaborate effectively in a university setting.
